CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right elbow pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient injured his right elbow approximately one week ago while playing lacrosse with his children. The injury occurred during a throwing activity. Patient was struck multiple times with a lacrosse stick by his son during play. No fall was recalled. Pain is sharp in character, localized to the tip of the elbow, and radiates down the forearm. Pain occurs with any movement of the elbow. Patient attempted ibuprofen (Advil) for a couple of days and reports it provided some relief.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies chest pain and abdominal pain. Otherwise not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Diabetes mellitus
Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur (known)

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg daily
Metformin 500 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient plays lacrosse with his children, ages 13 and 10. Family follows a Mediterranean diet with low salt intake. Patient reports decreased dietary compliance during the pandemic but has since resumed adherence to low-salt diet.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Blood Pressure: 150/90 mmHg
Lungs: Clear bilaterally
Heart: Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur
Right Elbow: Pain to palpation over olecranon area, mild pain with flexion and extension, normal range of motion, mild swelling and bruising noted

RESULTS
Right elbow X-ray: Normal, no fracture, no bony abnormality
Blood glucose (patient-reported when checked): 80-100 mg/dL
A1C: Ordered

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right elbow contusion from lacrosse stick injury. Continue ibuprofen 800 mg twice daily. Ice 3 times daily for 20 minutes per application. Avoid playing lacrosse for the next couple of weeks. Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily for hypertension with current diet compliance. Continue metformin 500 mg daily for diabetes. Obtain A1C to assess glycemic control and determine if future medication adjustment is needed.
